title: Integral closure in a quasi-coherent algebra on an algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal A$ be a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras on the small etale site $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ whose underlying module is quasi-coherent [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. There exists a unique quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-subalgebra $\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal A$ such that, for every affine scheme $U$ etale over $X$, $\mathcal C(U)$ is exactly the set of elements $a\in\mathcal A(U)$ satisfying a monic polynomial with coefficients in $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$, acting through the structure map to $\mathcal A(U)$. The inclusion of this subalgebra is the inclusion into $\mathcal A$ on each such object.

source.place: Tag 0820 (lemma-integral-closure), with uniqueness from the values on affine objects of the small etale site.

proof.text: For each scheme object $U\to X$, restrict $\mathcal A$ to $U_{\mathrm{et}}$. The cartesian-chart equivalence makes this a quasi-coherent module with its canonical restriction identifications. The Zariski/etale equivalence identifies it with a quasi-coherent Zariski module $B_U$ on $U$; because the inverse is restriction to open subschemes, $B_U(W)=\mathcal A(W)$ on open $W\subseteq U$. Its ring operations and structure map are the restrictions of those of $\mathcal A$, so it is a Zariski algebra. Apply the scheme integral-closure theorem to obtain the actual subsheaf $D_U\subseteq B_U$ defined by stalkwise integrality. Its affine sections are the required integral closures. Write $F_U=(D_U)_{\mathrm{et}}$.

source.place: Tag 0820 (lemma-integral-closure), first paragraph of proof; Morphisms Tag 035F.

proof.text: For a morphism $f:U^{\prime}\to U$ over $X$, the scheme-test etale cancellation theorem says $f$ is etale. The cartesian comparison for $\mathcal A$, transported through the Zariski/etale equivalence, gives $f^*B_U\simeq B_{U^{\prime}}$ with the prescribed section maps. If $W\subseteq U$ and $V\subseteq f^{-1}W$ are affine opens, put $R=\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_U)$ and $T=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_{U^{\prime}})$. The affine pullback formula identifies $B_{U^{\prime}}(V)=T\otimes_R B_U(W)$ and $(f^*D_U)(V)=T\otimes_R D_U(W)$. Apply ring integral-closure etale base change: the latter maps isomorphically onto the integral closure of $T$ in the former, which is $D_{U^{\prime}}(V)$. These identifications are the maps $t\otimes d\mapsto t\,f^*d$ into the ambient algebra, not arbitrary abstract isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0820 (lemma-integral-closure), middle paragraph; affine verification of More on Morphisms Tag 081K (lemma-integral-closure-smooth-pullback), using Algebra Tag 03GE.

proof.text: The preceding affine maps agree on overlaps: after mapping to $B_{U^{\prime}}$, both send a local tensor $t\otimes d$ to $t\,f^*d$, and $D_{U^{\prime}}$ is a subsheaf. They therefore glue by the sheaf axiom to a map $f^*D_U\to D_{U^{\prime}}$. Its source is quasi-coherent by preservation of quasi-coherence under scheme pullback; its target is quasi-coherent by construction. The affine-cover isomorphism criterion makes this map an isomorphism. For composable $U^{\prime\prime}\xrightarrow{g}U^{\prime}\xrightarrow{f}U$, both comparison composites map $s\otimes(t\otimes d)$ to $s\,g^*(t)\,(fg)^*d$ in $B_{U^{\prime\prime}}$. The inclusion of $D_{U^{\prime\prime}}$ is injective, so the composites agree. The identity comparison sends $1\otimes d$ to $d$. Thus the comparisons satisfy the cocycle and identity conditions. The Zariski/etale comparison gives a cartesian family $(F_U)$ on the etale chart sites.

source.place: Tag 0820, middle paragraph, with the omitted affine-to-sheaf argument in Tag 081K written out.

proof.text: Apply the cartesian-chart equivalence to $(F_U)$ to obtain a quasi-coherent module $C$ on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$. The compatible inclusions into the restrictions of $\mathcal A$ descend to a module map $i:C\to\mathcal A$. To check that it is a sheaf inclusion, cover any scheme object by affine opens. On an affine object $U$, the open-section normalization of the Zariski/etale equivalence gives $C(U)=D_U(U)$, and $i_U$ is the literal inclusion of the integral closure into $\mathcal A(U)$. If two sections of $C$ have the same image, their restrictions to every member of this affine covering agree, so they agree by the sheaf axiom. Hence identify $C$ with its image subsheaf.

source.place: Tag 0820 (lemma-integral-closure), final paragraph; Properties of Spaces Tags 03LY and 03LZ.

proof.text: The image subsheaf is closed under the algebra operations: on every affine scheme object it is the integral-closure subalgebra, hence contains the structural scalars and is closed under addition, additive inverses and multiplication. For any scheme object, restrict two sections to an affine open covering; the sums and products there belong to $C$, agree on overlaps because $C\to\mathcal A$ is injective, and glue in $C$. The same reasoning gives the scalar action and unit. Every algebra law and the compatibility of restrictions is inherited from $\mathcal A$ by injectivity. Its underlying module is the quasi-coherent module already constructed. This proves existence, the asserted affine values, and the specified inclusion.

source.place: Tag 0820, subsheaf-of-algebras conclusion; ring closure is Tag 00GO (lemma-integral-closure-is-ring).

proof.text: For uniqueness, let $C^{\prime}\subseteq\mathcal A$ have the stated affine values. Given an object $U$ and a section $a\in\mathcal A(U)$, cover $U$ by affine opens $U_i$. Membership of $a$ in either subsheaf is equivalent to membership of every $a|_{U_i}$: the local lifts are unique since these are subsheaves, agree on overlaps, and glue by the sheaf axiom. On each $U_i$ both membership conditions mean exactly integrality over $\Gamma(U_i,\mathcal O_{U_i})$, so they coincide. The two subsheaves, their operations, and their inclusion maps are equal.

source.place: Tag 0820, uniqueness from affine objects and the sheaf axiom.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0820 (lemma-integral-closure), with its affine compatibility and uniqueness arguments expanded.

C : Subobject A, (C : X.CommAlgebraSheaf).toModule.IsQuasicoherent ∧ ∀ (U : X.EtaleSite), IsAffine (X.etaleForget.obj U) → ∀ a : A.right.obj.obj (op U), a ∈ Set.range ((Subobject.arrow C).right.hom.app (op U)) ↔ (A.hom.hom.app (op U)).hom.IsIntegralElem a
